TITLE: Home Use Storage Carousel- A mechanical solution to ease the inconvenience of elderly's and handicapped's daily life
DATE_TIME: Timeline September 2024- April 2025
VENUE: [unreadable]
ORGANISERS_AND_LOGOS: University of Hong Kong
PEOPLE_TEAMS_WINNERS: Head of Research Dr. CHOY MMY; Member Cheung Ming Yau; Mak Ka Tsun; Liu Shing Ho, Howard
ALL_TEXT: University of Hong Kong
Home Use Storage Carousel- A mechanical solution to ease the inconvenience of elderly's and handicapped's daily life
Introduction
Elderly and Handicapped experienced inconvenience such as reaching for goods and groceries.
The need for a safe and convenient domestic storage unit rises, as the risk of injuries increased during recent years.
This project aims to design and manufacture a home use storage carousel which can aid the elderly in storing household products and minimizing the chances of injury.
Project Objectives
To create a storage device that allows the user to take items from the cabinet at a fixed location.
To create a prototype to test all parameters and requirements needed.
To test for the possibility of mass production and commercialisation of the project.
Challenges Encountered and Corresponding Solutions
Slippage of Belt System
Insufficient contact between the rubber timing belt and the gear due to the belt being too loose.
Internal idlers and two shafts are constructed to the belt system to ensure that the tension of the belt is sustained when the gears are rotating.
Material Tolerance
Great manufacturing errors exists between components due to coarse manufacturing process like 3D printing that cannot be corrected by precise CAD Drawing.
A trial-and-error approach was used to test out the optimal distance between the components to serve its function.
Collision of Boxes
Changing of box dimensions results in collision of box mounts during rotation as the boxes experienced angular momentum.
The box mount is changed to a shorter height, which prevents the interference with the boxes and ensure no shaking during rotation.
Pulley Deformation
Pulley deformed due to stress concentrated on the pulley, as they carry most of the load from the whole system.
Two aluminium plates are installed on each side of the pulley so that it received most of the load from the system and prevented the pulley from being under high stress concentration.
Bending of Structure Frame
The bottom region of the structure frame suffered with bending. The frame is not rigid enough to prevent this occurrence.
Through simulating the FEA analysis, additional support beams were installed on the sides of the structure frame to prevent the deformation of the structure.
Major Features
The system consists of 5 major parts, Storage Cabinet, Transmission System Motor, Electrical Control Unit and Outer Frame.
With the usage of buttons, users can rotate the corresponding cabinet to desired position for goods collection.
Future Possible Upgrades and Modifications
Lubrication System
Factory Grade Tolerance
System Upgrades such as installing more motors
Conclusion
The home storage carousel system is believed to be a cost-effective method to solve the current existing problems encountered by elderly and disabilities.
This design is believed to worth investing more time and resources in the predicted outcome.

ALL_TEXT: Abstract
Sustainable farming is gaining traction in Asia to address weed challenges that hinder crop growth. Traditional weed control methods often rely on toxic chemicals that are unsustainable in the long term, negatively impacting soil health and reducing crop fertility. Therefore, there is an urgent need for innovative weed elimination methods that do not depend on these conventional solutions.
We propose a compact, versatile weed-killing device that easily attaches to various farming equipment, such as harrows, tractors, or ATVs. Utilizing an affordable camera and advanced computer vision, the device accurately detects weeds, which are then targeted by a laser based on gathered positional data. Housed in a lightweight unit powered by a compact processing unit, it ensures speed and efficiency.
Our innovative device offers a cost-effective solution for small farmers, enabling effective weed management without chemicals. This approach enhances crop yields, improves the quality of life for both farmers and consumers, and promotes environmental sustainability, supporting the transition to more sustainable farming practices.

Crowd Monitoring System
WHY MONITOR CROWDS?
By knowing the number, movement, and distribution of people in a space, informed decisions can be made.
A person in a hurry can buy lunch at the place with the shortest queue, facility managers can distribute their staff more effectively, and high-capacity venues can prevent overcrowding.

1. Checkpoint modules are installed on the ceiling facing directly down
2. Multiple modules are placed with slightly intersecting coverage to cover a larger area
3. Each module detects the humans within its coverage and send their coordinates to a central server to be combined.
THE CHECKPOINT MODULE
Aimed at extreme scalability and adaptability, our crowd monitoring system relies on a modular checkpoint system to cover areas of any size.

2. Background Subtraction
Takes the thermal image and subtracts the median temperature of each individual pixel over the past hour.
This effectively removes all non-moving heat sources and adjusts to environmental changes like weather and seasons.
3. Island Detection
The filtered image is run through a rudimentary algorithm to detect isolated peaks in temperature within a reasonable size and returns their position in frame.
This effectively detects the positions of all human-sized moving heat sources in frame.

Name of Student Interest Group (SIG):Engineering and Archaeology
Engineering Projects for making Archaeelogical Fieldwork Practice more Efficient and Accurate
ABOUT
Project Supervisor: Prof. Peter J. Cobb | pcobb@hku.hk | Student Leader: Mr. Hayk Azizbekyan | hayk@connect.hku.hk
This project aims to develop innovative engineering solutions to accelerate and enhance archaeological fieldwork processes. Leveraging prior research and existing equipment inventories within the Innovation Wing, the project will deliver a suite of prototype devices and software integrations that automate key excavation, cleaning, and documentation tasks. The project has a summer base in overseas country of Armenia. Students with practical projects may get invited to implement their work during the fieldwork.
KEY FOCUS AREAS
SMART EXCAVATION
CLEANING SOLUTIONS
DOCUMENTATION & INTEGRATION
WE ARE LOOKING FOR
- Engineers (hardware, robotic, embedded systems)
- Software Engineers (backend, frontend,data, AI/ML)
- Product & Program Managers
- UI/UX Designers
- Domain Expert (archaeology, field research, etc.)
WHY JOIN?
- Work on a meaningful, real-world impact project
- Collaborate with diverse, talented team
- Use and shape the latest technologies and equipment
- Grow your skills and make a difference in preserving our past

Presenters: Prof. Peter Cobb, Ms. Navya Gupta, Ms. Shuya Lu, Mr. Hayk Azizbekyan
Technology is increasingly important in studying humanities topics such as Archaeology. HKU helps lead a collaborative fieldwork project in Armenia every summer where we are excavating a fortress from 3,000 years ago. This project is a fertile ground for experimenting with various technologies including 3D Recording, Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, Machine Learning and many other technologies. While making innovations HKU students may also get a chance to join us in Armenia every summer!

ALL_TEXT: BACKGROUND OF PROJECT
Role-playing is one method used in training social work students.
Using a real client is risky.
Using professional counselors as clients is costly.
The students have to role-play the client ineffective
That’s why chatbot comes into play!
However, existing chatbots lack the ability to adapt their openness or attitude during conversations, making them appear unrealistic.
We propose a realistic role-playing client with systematic behavior shifting
OPENNESS ADJUSTMENT
Openness level is introduced to simulate the real counseling sessions, which clients starting reserved but gradually becoming more willing to share as trust builds.
Openness adjustment enables students to practice:
Early-stage resistance: Handling guarded or defensive responses.
Gradual disclosure: Encouraging trust through active listening and validation.
Openness Adjustment Mechanism (Guided by Social Work Experts)
Conversation progress: Openness increases with rounds of dialogue, like natural trust-building.
Student skills: Use of active listening, validation, and etc. influences the rate of disclosure.
TECHNIQUE CLASSIFICATION
To evaluate social work students’ conversational skills and performance, our system classifies key techniques used by students during interactions with the AI client.
Automated Conversation Classification:
Classifies dialogues into 22 key categories defined by social work experts.
Uses annotated client-social worker conversations as training data.
High-Accuracy Classification Methods:
Tests multiple approaches to optimize results, including in-context learning & supervised fine-tuning.
Actionable Feedback:
Generates a technique distribution report to pinpoint strengths/weaknesses.
ROLE-PLAYING AGENT
The constructed prompt which will be fed to the model consists of 2 parts.
1.Client’s profile and client’s background story -
provided by social worker, each with goals that students need to achieve
2.Openness prompt - informing the model how much and helpful it should respond
The prompt is designed and developed based on social workers’ feedback.
DEMO
FUTURE WORK
Our project will be expanded to incorporate many features, for more effective and engaging for social worker training.
Emotional depth: another adjustable dimension additional to openness level.
Speech to speech interaction: Voice input and output capabilities simulating verbal communication with real-life clients, with possible extension to the use of voice tone and pitch to enhance emotional realism
Improved accuracy: The chatbot will be progressively refined to provide more realistic answers, especially in a range of diverse scenarios.
Performance Evaluation: add features including conversation summaries and a performance analytics dashboard.

Challenges in Robotic Arm Adoption
Skill Gap: Most workers in traditional industries lack the programming skills needed to operate robotic arms.
Psychological Barrier: Employees often find robotic arms intimidating due to their complexity and the perception of losing control over tasks.
OVERVIEW
The system simplifies teleoperation using geometric constraints and error-tolerant design, enabling precise control while reducing user workload.
The CNC machine cleaning task, developed from the daily routine work of a local Public Transport Company (PTC) in Hong Kong, guides workers into the field of Robotics. Applying the proposed task, our solution makes teleoperation more intuitive, reliable, and user-friendly.

USER EXPERIENCE AND DISCUSSION
Bridging the Skill Gap:
Three PTC trainees tested our system and were able to clean CNC machine grooves independently after a brief introduction, without damaging the robotic arm. This demonstrates the system's effectiveness in simplifying robotic arm operation for non-experts.
Reducing Psychological Barriers:
Traditional teleoperation often leads to misalignment between user intention and robotic movement, causing unintended oscillations, collision risks, and a reduced sense of control.
Our constraint-adaptive system improves usability by aligning movements with geometric constraints, minimizing manual adjustments, and enabling smoother, more intuitive operation.

ALL_TEXT: Blind quadrupedal magic
Allowing legged robots to walk on different terrains without using visual data
Referenced paper for this project:
"DreamWaQ: Learning Robust Quadrupedal Locomotion With Implicit Terrain Imagination via Deep Reinforcement Learning"
Final Year Project by Soogon Kim
In this project, our team aimed to enable a quadruped robot to navigate various terrains without relying on visual input. To achieve this, we studied a paper called "DreamWaQ: Learning Robust Quadrupedal Locomotion With Implicit Terrain Imagination via Deep Reinforcement Learning" and utilized Beta Variational Autoencoder with a policy network to help robots interpret their surrounding environment using past proprioceptive data.
How it works:
the Encoder receives 5 proprioceptive past observations that can be obtained inside rovet's internal sensor. The , the encoder produces a vector "z" that represents robot's imagination of the environment. Finally, based on the vector z, the policy produces 12 angle joint values for the robot to move.

ALL_TEXT: HERE WE TURN BACTERIA INTO GREEN MARKETABLE BENEFIT
Let's help make the world a better place
1.
SOLAR-POWERED
ELECTRON TRANSPORT
Integrate a synthetic photosystem (NPM) into E.coli membrane.
• Components: NuoK, PufL, MgP (light-
capturing pigments).
• Action: Light energizes electrons → boosts NADH production + generates formaldehyde (from methanol).
MgP synthesis
NuoK + pufL
C1 module
2.
GLUTATHIONE SURGE
Optimize cellular
detox for formate synthesis.
• Genetic Edits: Knock out gpmA; overexpress gshA + gshB.
• Result: Skyrockets reduced glutathione (GSH) levels → converts formaldehyde to formate.
3.
FORMATE FLOODGATE
Channel formate into hydrogen production.
• Mechanism: Formate (from Step 2) accumulates → feeds into the Formate Hydrogen Lyase (FHL) complex.
4.
CRISPR-ENHANCED
HYDROGEN CONVERSION
Precision integration of hydrogen-
generation machinery
• CRISPR Application: Engineered plasmid with formate → H2 gene
• Impact: Optimized FHL complex efficiency for maximal H2 yield
5.
HYDROGEN BURST!
Turbocharge FHL efficiency.
• Genetic Edits: OverExpress fhlA; knockout iscr + hycA (repressors).
• Result: FHL converts formate → H2 + CO2 at record rates.
OUR SCIENTIFIC PRINCIPLE
We engineered E.coli with a novel light-harvesting system (NPM) inspired by photosynthetic bacteria. By embedding NuoK (electron transporter), PufL (reaction center), and MgP (chlorophyll analog), we created a light-dependent electron chain. This system uses methanol as an electron donor to produce formaldehyde and NADH—key precursors for hydrogen synthesis.
METABOLIC ENGINEERING MASTERY
• GSH Overproduction: Knocking out gpmA halts competing pathways, while gshA/gshB overexpression floods cells with glutathione. This traps formaldehyde as S-hydroxymethylglutathione, driving its conversion to formate.
• FHL Hyperactivation: Derepressing fhlA (activator) and removing iscr/hycA (inhibitors) unleashes the FHL complex. This enzyme system splits formate into H2 and CO2 with industrial-scale efficiency.

ALL_TEXT: The software was developed in 2 stages:

ALL_TEXT: Introduction
ALL_TEXT: Large language models (LLMs) play a central role in our daily lives, and its integration has revolutionized processes
ALL_TEXT: This has been used in many applications such as customer support, education, with some even using it for chatbots for mental health.
ALL_TEXT: However, a shortcoming in the use of such models for counselling purposes is that, while it is able to simulate empathy through language, the responses are safe but generic that ignores specific nuances or factors (i.e. an inability to read between the lines). It is therefore unable to provide true "genuineness" specific to a client.
ALL_TEXT: We therefore introduce our model Heartful to overcome such limitations, where it is created to provide remedial counselling services with psychotherapeutic concepts in mind.
ALL_TEXT: Future directions include the offering of tools such as grounding exercises, cognitive reframing prompts, and behavior planning, while maintaining a supportive, non-judgmental tone. We thus discuss the impact of AI on counselling techniques.

ALL_TEXT: The entire application heavily relies on web3.js to manage the communication between web application and Ethereum. Via the digital wallet MetaMask, web3 can interact with smart contracts deployed on the local Ethereum or Ropsten test network. A hybrid data storage is achieved by using Cloudinary for storing the actual image, and the blockchain for storing the access link that is only retrievable with the hash key of user and image identifiers. Front-end rendering is done by React, which fetches from Express REST APIs on Node.js server

ALL_TEXT: How is "perserving originality" achieved?
ALL_TEXT: Proved by blockchain transaction
ALL_TEXT: All uploads are transactions done via Metamask with logged in account, thus are traceable and immutable records that prove originality
ALL_TEXT: Accessibility with unique hash
ALL_TEXT: Any attempted tampering will result in unsuccessful retrieval as it fails to provide the authentic identifier of user and image

ALL_TEXT: This modular underwater ROV features a modular, multifunctional design for flexible deployment in complex underwater environments. ALL_TEXT: Founded in 2025, Aqua focuses on developing flexible, cost-effective ROVs for harsh underwater environments. ALL_TEXT: Medical appointment scheduling is a challenging problem for hospitals and clinics due to the multi-dimensional stochasticity in practice, such as patient no-shows, patient unpunctuality, and non-deterministic service times.; An inefficient appointment schedule can lead to wastes of valuable resources (e.g., physician times) and long patient waiting times.; In this project, we developed a stochastic mixed-integer linear programming model to optimize medical appointment schedules.; OT (minute); IT (minute); WT (minute); No-show rate; Standard deviation (minute); Effects of patient no-shows and variations in service times on key performance indicators (KPIs) such as physician overtime and idle time and patient waiting time.; Capacity; Minutes (for OT, IT and WT); Analyses of the benefits of the optimization of appointment schedules, tradeoffs among different KPIs, and changes in KPIs using a dynamic capacity scheme.

TYPE: poster
TITLE: Emergency Department Operations Management
DATE_TIME: [unreadable]
VENUE: [unreadable]
ORGANISERS_AND_LOGOS: [unreadable]
PEOPLE_TEAMS_WINNERS: [unreadable]
ALL_TEXT: Emergency Department (ED) overcrowding is a long-standing and serious issue confronting many countries and cities. ED overcrowding can lead to numerous grievous consequences, including prolonged pain and suffering, patients’ dissatisfaction, and, most importantly, delay in the delivery of appropriate medical care to emergency patients. In this project, we apply OR techniques (analytical modeling and systems simulation) and data analytics for analyzing and improving ED operations in Hong Kong.
Simulation model calibration by optimizing the consistency measure through simulation optimization
c(x^{ab},\bar{x}) = \gamma_1 \sum_k w_{1,k} \frac{|\mu_k^{ab}-\bar{\mu}_k|}{\mu_k} + \gamma_2 \sum_k w_{2,k} \frac{|\sigma_k^{ab}-\bar{\sigma}_k|}{\sigma_k} + (1-\gamma_1-\gamma_2)\sum_k w_{3,k}\sum_j \frac{|p_{k,j}^{ab}-\bar{p}_{k,j}|}{p_{k,j}}
The detailed simulation model captures all relevant treatment processes (e.g., triage, consultation, lab tests), the complexities of intertwining and re-entrant patient-flows, time-varying and category-dependent patient arrival rates, and adjustable staff deployment.
